# `content/` — everything the site publishes, one file at a time

*Part of the [project library](https://whatsapp-voice-transcription.sgraph.ai/library/) — every doc behind this product, organised by audience.*

This folder is the **source of truth for published content**. The pages under
`website/updates/`, `website/videos/` and the data behind `website/versions/` are
**build output** — generated by [`scripts/build_content.py`](../scripts/build_content.py),
never committed, never edited by hand.

## The one rule

> **Publishing is adding one file. Nothing else.**

No index to update, no HTML to splice, no place to decide where a post goes. Ordering,
links, ids, markup, the JSON manifests and the RSS feed are all derived at build time.
Two agents publishing on the same day touch two different files and cannot conflict.

## Layout

```
content/
├── updates/YYYY/MM/DD/<version>__update__<slug>.md   a post — the public story
├── versions/<version>.md                             a release — the complete list
└── videos/<slug>.md                                  a video — demo, explainer or short
```

## Frontmatter

Flat `key: value` lines between `---` fences. Lists are comma-separated. No nesting,
no YAML parser, nothing to get subtly wrong.

### An update post

```markdown
---
title: The chat can now rewrite what's on the page
date: 2026-08-06                 # required, YYYY-MM-DD, must match the folder
version: v0.1.20                 # optional — adds the "what changed" diff link
issues: 035, 034                 # optional — adds "issue NNN — the full write-up" links
tags: chat, infographic          # optional — rendered as chips
status: published                # or: draft (written, held back from the build)
---

Markdown body. Paragraphs, `- ` bullets, `1. ` numbers, ## headings, **bold**,
*italic*, `code`, > quotes, ``` fences, and [links](/app/).
```

**You never write a GitHub URL.** Give the build a `version:` and it derives the diff
against the previous release; give it `issues:` and it finds each issue file *wherever
it currently lives* and links there. This is not convenience — hand-written links went
stale the moment an issue moved `open/ → done/`, and one shipped pointing at a branch
that keeps moving.

Internal links must be root-relative (`/app/`, `/versions/`), never `../`, because the
same markdown is rendered into pages at different depths.

### A version

```markdown
---
version: v0.1.20
date: 2026-08-06
title: Chat with your materials — and let it do the work
---

- One bullet per change, in plain language, for someone who does not read code.
```

### A video

```markdown
---
title: Chat with Your WhatsApp Voice Memos & Infographics
date: 2026-08-06
kind: demo                       # demo | explainer | short
duration: 2:23                   # optional, m:ss
youtube_id: dQw4w9WgXcQ          # the 11 characters from the watch URL
version: v0.1.20                 # optional — ties the video to a release
status: published                # a published video MUST have a valid id
---

A sentence or three of context — what the viewer will see.
```

Write the video file the moment you know it exists. If the id is not to hand yet, leave
`youtube_id:` empty and `status: draft`: the build holds it back rather than shipping a
dead player, and publishing later is a two-word edit.

## Working on it

```bash
python3 scripts/build_content.py --check     # validate everything, write nothing
python3 scripts/build_content.py             # build into website/ to preview locally
node --test tests/unit/content.test.mjs      # the same validation, as a test
```

CI runs `--check` in the test gate (bad content fails the build *before* a release) and
the full build in both deploy jobs, ahead of the cache-buster.

## What the build produces

| Output | What it is |
|---|---|
| `website/updates/index.html` | the Updates page, posts newest first, each with a `#slug` permalink |
| `website/updates/updates.json` | the manifest: every post's metadata and summary |
| `website/updates/feed.xml` | RSS, the 20 most recent posts |
| `website/videos/index.html` | the Videos page, grouped by kind, click-to-load players |
| `website/videos/videos.json` | the video manifest, so any page can show the latest |
| `website/versions/versions.json` | what the Versions page fetches |

## Adding a new kind of content

The build is a small script with one loader per type. A new type (say
`content/notes/`) is a `load_notes()`, a template, and a couple of lines in `build()` —
the layout, validation and manifest patterns are already there to copy. Agents keep
writing one file at a time.
